blocks.raw: <Tip>Memorize the critical distinction: Stirrups are in _beams_ (shear resistance). Ties are in _columns_ (confinement and bar stability). Spirals are continuous helical reinforcement in circular columns—much stronger than tied columns. Grade 60 is standard in the Philippines; yield strain ≈ 0.0021.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={[ "Confusing stirrups and ties. Stirrups are transverse reinforcement in beams perpendicular to longitudinal bars; they resist shear. Ties are transverse reinforcement in columns; they confine the core and prevent bar buckling. The terms and functions are distinct.", "Using Grade 60 yield strain = 0.003 (wrong). The correct value is 0.00207 ≈ 0.0021. This error propagates through strain-based design (balanced section calculations) and can lead to incorrect section classifications.", "Forgetting that steel modulus E = 200,000 MPa for all grades. Grade 40 and Grade 60 have the same E; only the yield stress (_F_y) differs. Confusion here affects curvature and deflection calculations.", "Placing stirrups in columns or ties in beams. This fundamental confusion reverses the structural system—stirrups in columns do not confine the core, and ties in beams do not resist shear effectively. Design intent is violated." ]} />
